title: refactor(shared): move the EPS to CSP address 1 and the SBC to 24
body:
Refs #120. #160 closes it, once #159 has widened the liveness mask and MCU-1 and MCU-2 move into the small node band.

The EPS is the one node present in every configuration of the stack, so it takes the fixed point of the addressing scheme: EPS moves from 4 to 1. The SBC moves from 1 to 24, the first slot of the large node band. It is the node that tracks liveness rather than one of the tracked nodes, so nothing ties it to the system band. MCU-1 and MCU-2 keep 2 and 3 for now, provisionally, and the header says so.

The header also carries the band allocation from #120, with the ground station at 40.

## Surface

Every literal that named an address: `node_ids.h`, the `McuNode` enum in `CspBridge.fpp` and its channel comment, the two EPS overlays and their header comments, `tests/e2e/check_protocol.py`, two lines in `eps-socketcan.resc`, and the documents, which are sections 3.1, 3.2 and R14 of BAC-FSW-SDD-001, the sample boot log in BAC-FSW-SUM-001, Appendix B of BAC-FSW-TN-001, two notes in BAC-FSW-TP-001, section 8 of BAC-SBC-SDD-001 and BAC-SBC-TN-002.

Everything else follows the symbols and needed no edit: `CspInterface.cpp`, the routing switch and `TRACKED_NODES` in `CspBridge.cpp`, the small node service layer and the CspBridge unit tests all address nodes through the macros.

Appendix B of BAC-FSW-TN-001 listed 1 SBC, 2 EPS, 3 MCU-1, 4 MCU-2, which never matched the header in any revision. It now carries the same scheme as everything else.

## The controller is a role

Small nodes reached the SBC two ways: the heartbeat through `CONFIG_BAC_PEER_ADDRESS`, and the HK publisher, FDIR alerts and power alerts through `BAC_NODE_SBC`. All four now go to the configured peer, so the controller is a role a node is configured with rather than an address compiled into it, and section 3.1 of BAC-FSW-SDD-001 says so. For the EPS nothing changes on the wire, since its peer is 24.

## The liveness mask

`aliveNodes` is a `U8` with bit n meaning node n, so only addresses 0 to 7 have a bit. A `static_assert` over the tracked addresses turns a node above 7 into a build failure instead of a silent gap. Widening the channel changes the dictionary and is #159.

## Validation

Validation on d73cdc1 with the main fix from #162 merged in: the CI matrix 25 of 25, F Prime native, unit tests 3 of 3, aarch64, and the e2e run in Renode with the corrected checker, 29 of 29 over 130 frames. The EPS addresses 24, the SBC addresses 1, and the header extensions carry 1 and 24. The e2e ran with the deployment's clock started on 15 September: on an October date Renode 1.16.1's RTC model kills the EPS a second into the run, see #161.
